name: Applied Combinatorics (Mitchel T. Keller and William T. Trotter)
goodFor: A combinatorics and graph theory textbook with exercises: counting, induction, graphs, posets, inclusion-exclusion, generating functions, recurrences and discrete probability.
attribution: "Mitchel T. Keller and William T. Trotter, Applied Combinatorics", linked to https://rellek.net/book/app-comb.html, with the section named; "CC BY-SA 4.0", linked to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; and, when the text shown was shortened or changed, a note that it was.

evidence.quote: This work is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License.
At Georgia Tech, MATH 3012: Applied Combinatorics, is a junior-level course targeted primarily at students pursuing the B.S. in Computer Science.
We feel that the topics of Chapters 1–9 plus Chapters 12, 13 and 14 are the core of a one semester course in Applied Combinatorics.

notes: Checked against the book's Colophon on the authors' site (edition 2017.3, copyright 2006–2025 Keller and Trotter): CC BY-SA 4.0 for the work, which allows commercial use; what Ceder changes stays under that licence. No per-chapter or per-figure exceptions were seen on the Colophon, Acknowledgements or Prefaces; figures weren't checked one by one. The colophon names appliedcombinatorics.org as the edition website, and a Runestone copy exists; neither was reachable or read, nor any terms of use for them, and rellek.net's home page returned an error, so no site terms were found. The book embeds SageMathCells, a third-party service. Its preface says it was written for a junior-level Georgia Tech course taken after calculus and some linear algebra, though its proofs are pitched below upper-division level; the early chapters (counting, induction, graphs) fit a lower-division discrete mathematics course, the later ones go beyond it. The bank's agents don't read it and nothing from it goes into the bank.
